stories.title: Ocarina of Time remake datamine suggests Master Quest is on the way
stories.summary: Ocarina of Time 's notoriously tricky Master Quest mode could be making a comeback in the new remake. Read more

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Ocarina of Time remake datamine suggests Master Quest is on the way
sources.text: Ocarina of Time's notoriously tricky Master Quest mode could be making a comeback in the new remake. Dataminer MrCheeze shared a list of strings from the remake's files on Bluesky, several of which tie the tag "MQ" to dungeons like Dodongo's Cavern. In a follow-up, as spotted by TheGamer , they pointed to further entries, including "HasMQ", "IsMQModeExist", "NewGameMQ", and "ReleaseMQ". Fellow dataminer OatmealDome added on Twitter/X that the mode will be unlocked by owning DLC, rather than arriving in an update, though "the data is incomplete". "I can confirm that the world is mirrored and dungeons are modified (e.g. cows in Jabu-Jabu's Belly)," they said. If you've not played it, Master Quest is a remixed version of Ocarina of Time with rearranged dungeons and tougher puzzles. It first appeared as a bonus disc on GameCube, then came back in 2011's Ocarina of Time 3D , which unlocked it after you finished the main game. That version also mirrored the whole world, which matches what OatmealDome has found, and had enemies deal double damage. [Ocarina of Time] #ootspoilers There is data in the game files for Master Quest. It will be unlocked by *owning DLC* - it is not just an update. The data is incomplete, but I can confirm that the world is mirrored and dungeons are modified (e.g. cows in Jabu-Jabu's Belly). As with any datamine, there's no guarantee it'll ever see the light of day. Nintendo hasn't announced any DLC for the remake, and it's not clear whether Master Quest would be free, like it was on 3DS, or paid. The Ocarina of Time remake launched on Switch 2 on 5th November. Donlan called the new version an "astonishing remake" in his five-star Eurogamer Ocarina of Time review .

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake files may hint at Master Quest DLC and Majora's Mask remake
sources.text: A third unknown Amiibo mask that characters refer to as "otherworldly" certainly feels like something The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake reportedly features files that not only tease a Master Quest expansion for the remake but also a Majora's Mask remake. While The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has done very well in terms of reception – having the highest Metacritic score of 2026 and the highest-ever user score on the site – there has been one bit of criticism leveled at it through most reviews of the game. Namely, the remixed Master Quest – which debuted with the GameCube port of the game and was later included in the 3DS remake by default – is not present in this remake. While many assumed Nintendo would be saving it as post-launch DLC – given Nintendo has readily adopted DLC since the 3DS – some evidence has emerged lending that theory some credibility. BlueSky user MrCheeze dug into the files of the game and found references to the mode, with strings of the game's code labeled with "MQ," with a screenshot showing references to "DodongoCavern" and "DodongoCavern_MQ." The questions now are: will this be free or paid DLC, and will this be a version of the original Master Quest – which has a bit of a mixed reception within the Zelda community – or will Nintendo have put as much work into the expansion as it did for the main game? On top of that, the other major question about the remake is "when is Majora's Mask being remade?" And while some pointed to the Happy Mask Salesman wearing his gold bracelets that were only present in his Majora's Mask look and Skull Kid saying " My face is missing something " (which is actually a hint for the Skull Mask quest found in the game), there's seemingly some actual evidence to support it happening now. In the Ocarina of Time remake, characters react to whatever mask Link wears. The game features all the original masks from the N64 game, but will soon add two more when the Link and Zelda amiibo release in 2027. These masks will feature N64-style looks for Link and Zelda; however, reactions have seemingly been found for a third unrevealed mask in the game's files. YouTuber Austin John Plays released a video showing that Zelda and Link are referred to as Mask 101 and 102 in the game's files, with a third titled Mask 103 also present. This mask keeps being referred to by NPCs as "otherworldly" and "suspicious," and has other dialogue attached. Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week One notable piece is "Huh, is that mask rare? Maybe monsters would ignore me if I wore one of those…" which, as Reddit user "Old_people_fucking" points out, reflects the functionality of Majora's Mask when worn in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom. And it would make sense to drop a Majora's Mask amiibo alongside the release of a Majora's Mask remake, right? Frankly, even without all of this, I fully believe a Majora's Mask remake is inevitable. It would be the easiest slam-dunk Nintendo could do right now, given that the game quite literally reuses assets from Ocarina of Time – Cremia and Romani are two characters who reuse Malon's adult and child models, respectively, for example. The original Majora's Mask was released about two years after Ocarina of Time, and with 2027 rumored to host a new 3D Mario as well as Pokemon Winds and Waves, I could see 2028 bringing Majora's Mask. Although Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa has said there's more to come from The Legend of Zelda series next year to celebrate its 40th anniversary, hopefully Nintendo wants to stack 2027, and we get all three… I can dream. Check out our The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review . You can also read our Legend of Zelda Switch 2 stock live blog if you're keen to grab one of Nintendo's new consoles for the game's launch. Scott has been freelancing for over four years across a number of different gaming publications, first appearing on GamesRadar+ in 2024. He has also written for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, VG247, Play, TechRadar, and others. He's typically rambling about Metal Gear Solid, God Hand, or any other PS2-era titles that rarely (if ever) get sequels. sources.title: How to find Princess Ruto in the Ocarina of Time Remake
sources.text: Ruto, the Zora Princess, is missing in OOT, and you need to find her Princess Ruto in Zelda Ocarina of Time is a Zora monarch you need to find, as she has the Spiritual Stone of Water you need to open the Temple of Time and continue. But Ruto's location is unknown when you first arrive in Zora's Domain, much to the concern of her father. King Zora has no idea where to look, but don't worry: I'll show you where to find Princess Ruto's location in OOT, and how to track down the clues she's left behind. After reaching Zora's Domain, you need to track down the princess using the clues left behind. Here's all the steps involved. Lord Jabu-Jabu's belly is a dungeon in its own right, and while Ruto is found inside near the entrance, you'll have to physically carry her to the exit and through the puzzles and challenges ahead. There's nothing wrong with her – she just refuses to walk under her own power. Once you're out of this dungeon, you'll be able to complete the entire Zelda Ocarina of Time Mask Shop quest, so check out our guide on that! Or if you're hoping to get a heart container, check out our guide on how to win the Ocarina of Time Treasure Chest Game . © GamesRadar+. Not to be reproduced without permission. sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time pode receber modo Master Quest no Nintendo Switch 2
sources.text: O remake de The Legend of Zelda : Ocarina of Time para Nintendo Switch 2 pode receber o modo Master Quest, conhecido por apresentar uma versão mais desafiadora do clássico da Nintendo . Lançado em 5 de novembro, o jogo já começou a ser investigado por dataminers, que encontraram referências ao modo nos arquivos da nova versão. Segundo informações divulgadas pelo Nintendo Everything e pelo Polygon, o usuário MrCheeze identificou os primeiros indícios em 6 de novembro. No dia seguinte, o dataminer OatmealDome encontrou informações adicionais que sugerem que o conteúdo poderá ser desbloqueado por meio de um DLC. A descoberta não significa, entretanto, que a Nintendo tenha confirmado o lançamento de uma expansão. Master Quest é uma versão alternativa de Ocarina of Time que aumenta a dificuldade da aventura, principalmente por meio de mudanças nas masmorras e na disposição de inimigos e desafios. O modo apareceu originalmente como parte de um disco bônus distribuído com determinadas cópias de The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker , no GameCube. Posteriormente, foi incluído no remake de Ocarina of Time para Nintendo 3DS, podendo ser desbloqueado após a conclusão da campanha principal. Na versão para Switch 2, entretanto, Master Quest não estava disponível no lançamento. De acordo com OatmealDome, os arquivos encontrados no novo remake incluem referências a um mundo espelhado e a masmorras modificadas, características associadas ao modo. O dataminer também afirma que o conteúdo estaria vinculado à posse de um DLC, e não apenas à instalação de uma atualização gratuita. Os arquivos, porém, ainda estariam incompletos. Até o momento, a Nintendo não anunciou oficialmente Master Quest ou qualquer DLC relacionado ao remake. Em entrevista anterior ao IGN, o produtor da franquia, Eiji Aonuma, comentou sobre a possibilidade de conteúdos futuros, afirmando que a empresa procura manter espaço para que os desenvolvedores explorem novas ideias após o lançamento. A declaração não confirma que Master Quest esteja em desenvolvimento, mas indica que a Nintendo não descarta a possibilidade de novidades posteriores. Por enquanto, os indícios encontrados nos arquivos devem ser tratados como informações não oficiais. Também não há detalhes sobre uma possível data de lançamento ou preço do conteúdo. stories.title: Will Grand Theft Auto 6 break the internet?
stories.summary: Back in September 2025, the launch of Hollow Knight: Silksong crashed the digital storefronts of Nintendo, PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam, as players who had waited over eight years for a follow-up to 2017's Hollow Knight rushed to download the highly anticipated sequel. Read more

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Will Grand Theft Auto 6 break the internet?
sources.text: The launch of Hollow Knight: Silksong caused digital storefronts to crash. How will they cope with the launch of GTA 6 at 212GB? Back in September 2025, the launch of Hollow Knight: Silksong crashed the digital storefronts of Nintendo, PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam, as players who had waited over eight years for a follow-up to 2017's Hollow Knight rushed to download the highly anticipated sequel. The wait for a sequel to Grand Theft Auto 5 has been even longer – some 13 years – and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 will be orders of magnitude bigger than Silksong's. Silksong sold 7 million units in the first three months , reaching a peak of over half a million concurrent players a day after launch . GTA 6, by contrast, has already been pre-ordered by nearly 8 million players according to Sensor Tower estimates , with many more sales expected at launch on November 19. And whereas Silksong came in at a svelte download size of 8GB on Steam, GTA 6 weighs in at a whopping 212GB. Importantly, GTA 6 is also the first AAA blockbuster of this scale to launch as a digital-only release. When GTA 5 launched back in 2013, the focus of the games business was still largely physical – but this time around, everyone who wants to buy the game will have to download it. The pre-load period for GTA 6 starts at midnight on November 10 , ahead of the official launch on November 19. Will the PlayStation and Xbox digital storefronts hold up? And how will the internet more widely cope with the strain? GamesIndustry.biz asked a group of experts about what to expect. Joost van Dreunen, founder of Aldora and author of the SuperJoost Substack , points to the launch of Grand Theft Auto 5's online component in October 2013; it's not well remembered now, but it didn't go smoothly. "It effectively melted Rockstar's infrastructure, which ultimately didn't hurt the franchise, but did create a massive hiccup at the time," he says. The online component for GTA 6 is still further down the line, with just the single-player version launching next week, so Rockstar doesn't have to worry about its servers just yet – that's the platform holders' concern. "The heavy lifting sits with Sony and Microsoft, not Rockstar," says van Dreunen. He expects the platform holders will be adding plenty of server capacity, and the lack of other game launches around GTA 6 ( aside from a gung-ho few ) will help to ease the strain, along with the option to pre-load well ahead of release. It's likely that both Sony and Microsoft are pulling all the stops out behind the scenes. "Nobody wants to be the platform that fell over on the biggest launch in a decade." GamesIndustry.biz contacted both PlayStation and Xbox for comment, but neither has responded. However, an old Sony hand says there's good reason for optimism. Gordon Thornton spent 17 years at Sony, during which time he oversaw the development of PlayStation Network and the PlayStation Store, and he is now chief commercial officer at ZBD . He says that Sony is well equipped to deal with the infrastructure demands of GTA 6, having previously fallen short in the past. "If you go back as far as the first Call of Duty map packs, we were overwhelmed and learned the hard way," Thornton explains. "My claim to fame is we took out Apple and every other digital merchant working on Worldpay at the time with the first Call of Duty map pack, because the transactions per second on our payment gateway failed. Access-wise, however, we now understand that through a very sophisticated distributed architecture." Thornton says that in the years since, the option to pre-load games has eased the strain on download servers, as players can begin downloading huge files well before the day of release. And the fact that Rockstar started taking pre-orders back in June will no doubt help. Silksong, by contrast, only had its release date revealed a couple of weeks before launch , and there was no option to download the game ahead of time. "Silksong had no pre-orders, so the entire download and the entire purchase hit Steam and the console stores in the same minute, and the stores buckled," notes van Dreunen. Thornton adds that the sheer level of excitement surrounding Silksong "likely stumped" the platforms, but says that pre-loading will help manage demand for Grand Theft Auto 6. "Consoles load it up and download it gradually, ensuring the distribution network is not overloaded. When reaching the launch minute, it is just a key exchange, which is quick even with millions of downloads." Simon Carless, author of the GameDiscoverCo newsletter, says that the pre-orders and pre-load will "significantly alleviate pressure" on PlayStation and Xbox. "The pre-load is starting November 10, and requires up to 212 GB of local drive space, so that's very hefty," he explains. "So having an extra nine days to gradually send out the bulk of the data to players' computers is vital. There still might be a Day 1 patch/extra download, but if so, it'll be very incremental." But van Dreunen warns that the real bottleneck could come on launch day, which in contrast to Silksong, could see "tens of millions day-of buyers, not a few hundred thousand." Neil McRae, chief technology and innovation officer at UK internet provider CityFibre , says that although pre-loading will help to manage overall demand, "there's no getting away from the fact that launch day will be extremely busy, as many people will wait until launch to buy." There's also the question of what kind of pressure will be placed on the telecom infrastructure more broadly, as millions of people simultaneously cue huge downloads at launch. "For network providers, this will raise the peak transfer rate; essentially, the high traffic will drive record-breaking throughput," says McRae. But he thinks the network can handle it. "Whether it's the launch of GTA 6, or major Fortnite or Call of Duty updates, network spikes are now a common occurrence rather than an anomaly, and providers are well e

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival live event set for November 21
sources.text: Rockstar Games and Sony Interactive Entertainment will host “ Grand Theft Auto VI : The Festival ,” a special live event at Mana Wnywood in Miami, on November 21, the companies announced. The event will feature a “star-studded lineup” of artists from the game and official soundtrack, including two stages of “non-stop music” with performances by Cactus Jack presents Travis Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black, and Sofaygo; Cardi B; Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso; Justice (DJ set); Metro Boomin; Nick Leon B2B DJ Python; Prospa B2B Skream; Rauw & Friends; Suero; Tainy; The Dare B2B Fcukers (DJ set). A pre-sale lottery for a chance to purchase tickets will begin on November 11. Tickets are limited to two per pre-sale lottery. The lottery closes on November 10 at 1:00 p.m. PT / 4:00 p.m. ET. Users can sign up for the lottery here . Grand Theft Auto VI is due out for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series on November 19.

sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6: The Festival will include Travis Scott, Cardi B and Justice among others Rockstar has announced that a music festival based on Grand Theft Auto 6 will be taking place later this month. Grand Theft Auto 6 : The Festival will take place at Mana Wynwood in Miami, and will feature performances from such musical acts as Travis Scott, Kodak Black, Cardi B and Justice. “Experience the music of Vice City and Leonida at Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, a special live event on November 21 at Mana Wynwood in Miami to celebrate the launch of GTA VI, featuring a star-studded lineup of artists from the game and the official soundtrack,” Rockstar ‘s official description reads. The full list of artists confirmed to be taking part in the festival is as follows: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, a special live event on November 21 at Mana Wynwood in Miami to celebrate the launch of GTAVI, featuring a star-studded lineup of artists from the game and the official soundtrack. Two soundtracks are being released for Grand Theft Auto 6, both of which will be available in CD, vinyl and streaming. GTA 6: The Album , which will be released on November 19 alongside the game, will consist of 34 brand new, original tracks from âa genre-defying roster of the most exciting artists in the worldâ including Travis Scott and Keith Richards. Grand Theft Auto VI: Original Score , meanwhile, will be released on December 11 and will consist of 30 tracks taken from French electronic duo Justice’s full suite of material composed for the game.

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: GTA: Tokyo saw Rockstar negotiate with a Japanese studio, former Grand Theft Auto lead says
sources.text: The story likely would have been set in the present day, and it "definitely had samurai swords in it," says Obbe Vermeij Decades before GTA 6 , Rockstar Games was considering getting a Japanese studio to develop the now-abandoned GTA: Tokyo, according to a former technical director on the series, but he reckons that there's "so much Americana inherent in the IP" that it might not have worked, anyway. It sounds like we were so close – yet so far – from getting GTA: Tokyo. A trademark for the title was filed by Rockstar owner Take-Two Interactive back in late 2003, after the release of Vice City, but was later listed as abandoned in 2008. Over the years, we've found out the occasional bits of information about it – one anonymous former Rockstar dev allegedly claimed that the scrapping of the idea ultimately "just came down to logistics," with the tasks of mapping out the city and nailing the "cultural satire in terms of what could possibly work in a fitting narrative way in that city" proving rather difficult. Obbe Vermeij, a former technical director who left Rockstar in 2009, previously indicated that the game "almost actually happened," with another studio in Japan set to handle development, but that the idea of setting a game in "some left-field location for novelty" wouldn't work. Vermeij has now elaborated on this further in a new interview with Rock Paper Shotgun . Vermeij admits that the information was "above my pay grade," but that "there were negotiations with studios, and I have a name, but I'm not gonna say it, because then it becomes like a bigger thing than it is, and I'll probably get it wrong, and I don't know how far the negotiations were, how serious it was. I mean, it was definitely serious. It was the plan. But I don't know how close it got to actually happening." According to Vermeij, Tokyo's story likely would have been set in the present day, or at the very least, a time "not too [far off] – it wasn't, like, sort of the medieval era in Japanese history, or anything. It was definitely not like that." With that said, though, "it definitely had samurai swords in it," he says. Oh, what could have been. Tokyo wasn't the only city that Rockstar considered doing something with, according to Vermeij. Paris, Moscow, Rio de Janeiro, London, and Istanbul were frequently suggested internally, he says, but he muses that perhaps a full GTA game set outside of the US might not work very well anyway. "We always decided there was so much Americana inherent in the IP, it would be really hard to make it work in London or anywhere else," he explains. "You know, you needed guns, you needed these larger-than-life characters. It just felt like the game was so much about America, possibly from an outsider's perspective. But that was so much about what the thing was that it wouldn't really have worked in the same way elsewhere." Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more That's not to say he wouldn't have liked a Japanese GTA to happen, though. On the conception of the idea, Vermeij wonders if Rockstar co-founders Dan and Sam Houser "were a little annoyed that GTA wasn't as big in Japan as they thought it deserved to be," and therefore "it kind of made sense to get a local studio to do it." Regardless, though, he thinks "it would have been really cool, because you know, a GTA made by somebody else in Japanese culture – that's something I would probably play." GTA 6 launch files already hint at online multiplayer, PlayStation Store sleuth reports, leading to hopes we won't be waiting for a GTA Online follow-up for long. I'm GamesRadar+'s Deputy News Editor, working alongside the rest of the news team to deliver cool gaming stories that we love. After spending more hours than I can count filling The University of Sheffield's student newspaper with Pokemon and indie game content, and picking up a degree in Journalism Studies, I started my career at GAMINGbible where I worked as a journalist for over a year and a half. I then became TechRadar Gaming's news writer, where I sourced stories and wrote about all sorts of intriguing topics. In my spare time, you're sure to find me on my Nintendo Switch or PS5 playing through story-driven RPGs like Xenoblade Chronicles and Persona 5 Royal, nuzlocking old Pokemon games, or going for a Victory Royale in Fortnite. sources.title: London department store Selfridges launches sizeable GTA 6 takeover, featuring a varsity jacket that costs an eye-watering £2,500
sources.text: Expensive British department store Selfridges has launched a sizeable Grand Theft Auto 6 takeover, completely making-over its Oxford Street London Corner Shop store and offering a considerable line of clothing, which includes an exclusive varsity jacket that costs a bank-melting £2,500. Note, you can buy the GTA 6 items online as well. Live from Selfridges at Oxford Street for the #GTAVI activation🌴 Rockstar are not messing around 🤯 pic.twitter.com/vqqXKwB1oJ That GTA 6 varsity jacket is by far and away the most expensive item (and it's apparently already sold out), next to a non-exclusive varsity jacket that's £1,750, whereas the other items are pricey but conceivably affordable. There are a few ranges on offer. There's a nice bright teal and pink-coloured range based around the spoof NFL team the Vice City Manatees, which includes a manatee plushie, an American football, a jacket, and other bits and bobs. There's also a range based around the spoof NBA team, the Vice City Narcos, that includes a basketball (there's a standard GTA 6-branded basketball too). There's a range based on the spoof fast-food chain Burger Shot, which includes a visor, work uniform, and apron, amusingly. There are some admirably horrid postcard-decorated shirts and shorts, and there's a lot of generic game-branded caps and T-shirts besides, all in quite nice colours. Quirky branded offerings include an ashtray, money clip and dartboard. It's all quite attractive stuff. There's no word on how long the items will be stocked for or that the Selfridges Corner Shop takeover will run for, other than "while stocks last". Grand Theft Auto 6 arrives 19th November - next week - so the hype machine is now in full effect. GTA 6 pre-load dates, times and details have been announced, and we know what the GTA 6 Trophies and Achievements will be.

sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: GTA 6 Jacket That Costs $3,000 Immediately Sells Out
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 will be the biggest game of 2026, and Rockstar Games certainly knows it. The studio hasn’t missed a beat with promotional merch hyping the game, having previously sold a $400 collector’s edition that doesn’t include the game (which goes for at least $79.99). In its latest stunt, Rockstar partnered with the luxury British department store Selfridges for an all-out promotional event that opened earlier today. The installation at 400 Oxford Street features a Grotti Cheetah Classic painted in GTA 6 ’s blue-and-pink color palette, a Leonida alligator statue, and other Vice City-themed paraphernalia teasing the game’s locale. The event includes more than 60 GTA 6- themed items, including clothing, basketballs, mugs, luggage tags, and more, many of which are being sold exclusively at Selfridges. When the brick-and-mortar store opened, Selfridges also temporarily sold the merch online. As per IGN , the launch queue exceeded 100,000 people, and many products sold out. Among these sold-out items was a varsity jacket that went for a whopping £2,500 ($3,356). Yikes. The “Grand Theft Auto VI Goodtime State Varsity Jacket” has a Rockstar logo and “VI” emblazoned on the front, and “Vice City” text on the back next to the Macca the Gator, a flamingo with sunglasses, and a purple lowrider. If you need more evidence that the merchandise-collector craze has kicked into high gear, look no further than Rockstar's shrewd efforts. GTA 6 will be released for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series on Nov. 19 , where it will presumably become one of the highest-selling games of all time. The game became available to preload earlier today for those in New Zealand. Rockstar previously announced the game will take up to 212 GB, with the audio file alone taking up 22 GB. Data miners have already started digging into the preload files, with one reporting a variable called “launchMultiplayerActivity,” implying that GTA Online will eventually come to GTA 6 . In the United States, preloading will become available on Xbox and PlayStation between this afternoon and midnight.

sources.title: How to beat the Treasure Chest Game in Zelda Ocarina of Time
sources.text: The Treasure Chest Shop in the OOT Remake can be beaten with luck - or a special item The Treasure Chest Game in the Zelda Ocarina of Time remake has Link forced to pick between a pair of chests five times in a row, with a heart container as the potential reward. If you pick incorrectly at any point you lose, but there is a way (two ways, in fact) to beat the system and get this substantial reward early in the Switch 2 OOT remake. If you want to know how, I'll explain where to find the Treasure Chest Shop in Ocarina of Time, and how to beat the treasure chest game easily. Around the corner, you can find the Zelda Ocarina of Time Happy Mask Shop . Check out our guide on the quest tied to it, and how you can hand out the masks to those who need them! The Treasure Chest Shop in OOT is located on the West Side of Hyrule Castle Town, at the spot shown above. However, it can only be accessed at Night. If it's daytime and you don't want to wait, head North along the alley to the building with the blue door, which will have a bed you can rest in to change the time of day. The Treasure Chest Game is simple: you'll be shown a pair of chests, one of which is right, and one of which is wrong. If you pick correctly, you move forward to the next round. If you pick wrong, you lose the game. If you can pass five rounds, you'll get a heart container. The problem is, the chests looks identical, and each attempt costs you 10 Rupees. sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Is Scarier Than Ever on Switch 2
sources.text: When I first encountered The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time growing up, it scared the crap out of me. The screeching Redeads, the skittering spiders, the disembodied hands — it was basically a horror movie to a young kid’s eyes. I’m older and harder to spook now, of course, which means that I knew the Nintendo 64 game’s fresh Switch 2 remake was bound to hit differently. Surely I’d laugh at everything that used to creep me out and realize that I was scared of a glorified cartoon! How wrong I was. Ocarina of Time ’s remake is arguably even more of a horror show than its 1998 predecessor. Though some goofy voice acting might lure you into a false sense of security, the faithful remake uses the technical power of the Switch 2 for chaotic evil. Every creepy crawler that may have freaked you out in the ‘90s has gotten whatever the opposite of a glow-up is. The remake is terrifying — and I am in full support of that evil creative decision. The important thing to understand about Ocarina of Time if you're totally new to it is that it has the energy of a Grimms’ fairy tale . You know, the kind that revolves around an evil witch who cooks children alive. Kind of whimsical, kind of messed up. For every funny little moment in Ocarina of Time , like a scooting Zora king or a dancing Goron, you’ve also got a quest where you have to drop into a man’s grave after learning he died after Link traveled forward in time. It’s dark, though in a very family-friendly Nintendo way. That said, the remake really emphasizes just how unnerving the original game can be. Nintendo didn’t hold back when redesigning some of its scariest monsters. Take Redeads, for instance. The creatures are essentially zombies that lurch towards Link slowly, but can paralyze him with fear by letting out a blood-curdling screech. If they catch him, they can wrap around his little head and squeeze the life out of him, a traumatizing image for a ‘90s kid. That all holds true in the remake, except now you can also see every branch-like vein across the skin on their rotten, wooden bodies. Their faces are nightmare fuel too, with more detail put into the red mask that hides whatever is happening up there. Better if I don’t know, I reckon. Deku Babas? Those now have crooked, gnashing teeth and tongues that look like overgrown gourds. Gibdos? They went from looking like basic mummies to Curly from Mouthwashing , with a dead eye peeking out from rough bandages. Floormasters? The sentient hands now have protruding bones, just to screw with you. Moblins? They have butt cheeks now. (That part isn’t scary, it’s just kinda weird, I suppose.) Everything is a grotesque little freak that I would like to squash with a hammer. And then, there are the spiders. Be warned: Readers with arachnophobia might want to stop reading here. Ocarina of Time ’s Skulltulas have always been the series’ most skin-crawling monsters. They’re basically giant spiders with cracked skulls for bodies. Predictably, they are abominations here, thanks to their furry little legs that make them even grosser. Gold Skulltulas are equally disgusting, even though Nintendo toned down their loud skittering sounds that made them especially scary in 1998. But what’s really been brought to a whole new circle of hell is the House of Skulltula. It’s home to a cursed family who have been transformed into Skulltulas, turning each of them into a half-spider, half-man situation straight out of The Fly . They look so horrific in the remake that you will wish you could put them out of their misery. You can see their warped faces under their skull bodies. They each have a human arm dangling off their spider legs. It’s the most hellish sight I have ever seen in a kid’s game, and I am proud of Nintendo for allowing it to happen. Not everything about the remake is scarier. Like Likes are still slimy little freaks, but their additional detail makes them less scary than the unknowable blobs of the original game. Hyrule Castle Town is less unnerving post-time skip now that the original game’s Resident Evil-like fixed camera angles are no more. In general, the overall atmosphere of the remake skews more towards that of an animated cartoon, which takes some bite out of the N64 version. I still prefer the original game, with its low-poly textures and more muted colors, for that reason. Even so, the commitment to creepiness is just one of the reasons that Nintendo’s remake works so well. It understands what made the original game special, and works to amplify that vibe rather than wash it away. It’s similar to how developer Grezzo handled its Link’s Awakening remake, leaning on toy-like design and whimsy to retain the lightness of the original game. The most important — and hardest — thing to get right in a remake is aura, and Ocarina of Time nails the assignment in that respect.

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Tripwire Interactive lays off 36
sources.text: The cuts are the studio's second round of layoffs this year Killing Floor and Maneater developer Tripwire Interactive has laid off 36 staff. In a statement posted to Twitter/X today, the studio said: "Today we share difficult news: Tripwire has undergone a workforce reduction, affecting 36 talented people across our studio. This was certainly not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organization." Tripwire said its remaining staff are focused on internal projects, including "active development of Maneater 2, ongoing work on Killing Floor 3 and publishing efforts under the Tripwire Presents label," adding that it would support those affected "with compassion and dignity during this transition." The layoffs come just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support smaller self-published indie developers . It's the second round of layoffs this year , after 23 staff were laid off in March. Tripwire was founded in 2005 by John Gibson and Alan Wilson. Gibson stepped down as CEO in 2021 following anti-abortion comments , with Wilson taking on the role of interim CEO. In 2022, the developer was acquired by the Embracer Group via its former subsidiary Saber Interactive . Former CFO Matthew LoPilato was promoted to CEO in 2024. Embracer sold Saber Interactive for $247 million in 2024 but kept Tripwire.

sources.name: Insider Gaming
sources.title: Killing Floor 3 Developer Tripwire Interactive Announces Layoffs
sources.text: Another round of layoffs hit the video game industry today as Tripwire Interactive, the studio behind Maneater and Killing Floor, announces a workforce reduction. This news came while Tripwire Interactive is in the middle of development for Maneater 2. The layoffs will see 36 people let go from the studio. The reduction was announced on Tripwire Interactive’s accou n t on X (formerly Twitter) on November 9, 2026. The studio shares that the staff let go will be supported through the transition. While an official reason hasn’t been given, Tripwire did share that it was, “not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organization.” This is the second time this year Tripwire has laid off employees, the first time being in March . This puts the total of laid-off employees at 59 this year. As of now, there is no reported effect on the development of Maneater 2. Tripwire says in their announcement, “Our team is focused on our internal projects including active development of Maneater 2, ongoing work on Killing Floor 3 and publishing efforts under the Tripwire Presents label.” The game is set to release in 2027 with no official release date yet. Do you think the layoffs at Tripwire Interactive will impact Maneater 2? Let us know down in the comments and in the official Insider Gaming Discord . sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: A week after expanding its publishing division, Killing Floor studio Tripwire Interactive lays off 36 people
sources.text: Tripwire said the decision to put people out of work was "a necessary one for the organization." Killing Floor studio Tripwire Interactive has laid off 36 employees in what it says "was certainly not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organization." The cuts at Tripwire appear significant: A source at the studio told PC Gamer that roughly 40-50 employees are left following the layoffs. "Our team is focused on our internal projects, including active development of Maneater 2, ongoing work on Killing Floor 3, and publishing efforts under the Tripwire Presents label," the studio wrote in a message shared on LinkedIn . "We are continuing to give the best support possible to all of our games and remain committed to our awesome community." Maneater 2 was announced in September, five years after the release of the original, which was a significant success for Tripwire. But the studio has had difficulty replicating that success, even with its best-known game series: Killing Floor 3, released in 2025, remains mired in "mixed" user reviews on Steam , and its concurrent player count on the platform is a small fraction of its 2016 predecessor. The layoffs also come less than a week after Tripwire announced an expansion of its Tripwire Presents publishing division to include "scaled publishing support of smaller independent developers"—essentially offering a variable suite of services to what Tripwire publishing director Bryan West called "scrappy developers" who could a little assist with their games in specific areas. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. stories.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: a atualização com novo jogo+, novo recurso e muito mais
stories.summary: The post Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: a atualização com novo jogo+, novo recurso e muito mais appeared first on Xbox Wire em Português .

sources.name: Xbox Wire BR
sources.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: a atualização com novo jogo+, novo recurso e muito mais
sources.text: A atualização mais pedida de Assassin’s Creed Valhalla já está disponível no XBOX Series X|S e no XBOX One. A atualização traz diversas novidades empolgantes ao jogo, oferecendo novas maneiras de aproveitar sua aventura viking. O grande destaque é a chegada do Novo Jogo+, um dos recursos mais pedidos pelos fãs de Assassin’s Creed Valhalla . As demais novidades do patch garantem que sua experiência após o fim da campanha e no Novo Jogo+ seja renovada e desafiadora, com recompensas que fazem tudo valer a pena. Confira o que esperar da atualização mais pedida: Conversamos com o designer-chefe de jogo, David Larouche, para saber mais sobre a atualização e como a equipe coloca os jogadores no centro de tudo o que faz. Quais novidades desta atualização são uma resposta direta aos comentários da comunidade? David Larouche : o Novo Jogo+ foi, sem dúvida, o recurso mais pedido pelos fãs. Assassin’s Creed Valhalla é um jogo imenso, mas, para algumas pessoas, jogar uma vez só não basta. Com esta atualização, estamos muito empolgados em permitir que nossos vikings mais dedicados vivam essa aventura novamente, mas, desta vez, com o personagem que tinham ao final da campanha. Como a equipe garantiu que os recursos pedidos atendessem às expectativas dos jogadores? DL : queríamos que a experiência do Novo Jogo+ não fosse apenas jogar tudo de novo; queríamos permitir que os jogadores continuassem aumentando seu poder, percebessem uma progressão em etapas menores e seguissem aprimorando seus personagens. Por todos esses motivos, adicionamos um modo de progressão estendida, mais melhorias para todas as peças de equipamento divino, uma nova categoria de runas e mais de 300 novas opções de bônus de runas que podem ser gravados na Forja de Runas — e todos esses recursos também estão disponíveis fora do Novo Jogo+. Com todas essas novidades, acreditamos que a experiência do Novo Jogo+ incentivará os jogadores a explorar todo o potencial de Eivor. Houve algum desafio inesperado na implementação dessas novidades? DL : acho que o mais surpreendente para nós foi justamente não termos encontrado nenhum grande desafio que nos deixasse sem saber como avançar. Conseguimos reunir uma equipe muito competente de desenvolvedores com experiência em adicionar o Novo Jogo+ a jogos já existentes; o processo de produção foi incrivelmente tranquilo. Há algum recurso que você esteja especialmente empolgado para ver no jogo? DL : com a atualização, transformamos praticamente todos os bônus presentes em itens em runas que podem ser gravadas na Forja de Runas, independentemente de terem sido lançados na experiência estendida, em uma expansão ou até mesmo na Loja. Mal posso esperar para ver como os jogadores vão combinar todos esses bônus e criar os mais variados tipos de sinergia. Tenho certeza de que há muitas combinações poderosíssimas a serem descobertas! Assassin’s Creed Valhalla recebeu sua última atualização de conteúdo há anos. Por que lançar a atualização mais pedida para os jogadores agora? DL : Valhalla pode ter recebido sua última atualização de conteúdo há anos, mas isso não significa que os jogadores deixaram de se importar com o jogo — e nós também não. Sabemos que o Novo Jogo+ é algo que a comunidade deseja há muito tempo e, quando surgiu a oportunidade de finalmente torná-lo realidade, mal podíamos esperar para seguir em frente. No fim das contas, trata-se de dar aos jogadores de longa data mais um motivo para voltar a um mundo ao qual dedicaram tanto tempo e reviver a jornada de Eivor sob uma nova perspectiva, levando consigo boa parte do que conquistaram pelo caminho. O fato de algum tempo ter passado não torna essa experiência menos significativa para nós nem, esperamos, para nossos jogadores. Qual é a importância da comunidade de Assassin’s Creed para a equipe da franquia? DL : a comunidade é extremamente importante para mim e para a equipe. Pessoalmente, acompanho as redes sociais com frequência para ver sobre o que os jogadores estão conversando e, como equipe, prestamos muita atenção aos comentários e às conversas pela internet. Adoramos ver o que os jogadores criam e compartilham sobre nossos jogos. Essa conexão com a comunidade é incrivelmente gratificante e é uma das principais razões pelas quais fazemos o que fazemos. Jogue hoje mesmo Assassin’s Creed Valhalla com a atualização mais pedida no XBOX Series X|S e no XBOX One.

sources.title: Sonic Pico Park, Shrek 2 Remastered e mais! Veja os lançamentos de games da semana
sources.text: Mais uma semana que começa com a nossa lista de lançamentos para que você possa se programar para os próximos dias. O grande destaque dessa vez é Sonic Pico Park , game do icônico personagem em uma abordagem nunca antes vista, que mistura elementos de puzzle com cooperação entre os personagens. Outro destaque é Shrek 2 Remastered . Como o nome sugere, ele é uma remasterização de um dos games mais elogiados do famoso ogro dos cinemas, que conta com melhorias nos gráficos e no desempenho. Confira a lista completa de lançamentos da semana e os respectivos preços. Shrek 2 Remastered é uma versão remasterizada do jogo de aventura lançado originalmente para a geração 128 bits , no PlayStation 2 e Nintendo GameCube. O título acompanha o ogro e seus amigos em fases baseadas na história do segundo filme da franquia de animação, passando por locais como o pântano e o reino de Tão Tão Distante. A jogabilidade permite alternar entre quatro personagens durante as missões , cada um com habilidades específicas para resolver puzzles no cenário e avançar na história. O lançamento traz melhorias gráficas e suporte para resolução atualizada, além de manter o foco no modo cooperativo local para até quatro pessoas. O game já está em pré-venda a partir de R$ 87,29. Football Manager 27 é o novo capítulo da franquia anual de simulação e gerenciamento de futebol , que é desenvolvida pela Sports Interactive. O jogador assume o papel de treinador e gerente de um clube, e precisa lidar com as responsabilidades do cargo, d esde a montagem do elenco até o controle das finanças e o relacionamento com a imprensa. A edição deste ano atualiza os elencos, ligas e competições para a temporada atual do futebol mundial. O título oferece ferramentas de análise de dados para ajustar táticas antes e durante as partidas e traz sistemas de observação para contratar novos jogadores e desenvolver talentos nas categorias de base do time. OBS: Por motivos de licenciamento, o jogo não é vendido de forma oficial no Brasil. Warhammer Survivors é um jogo de ação com visão isométrica, inspirado no fenômeno Vampire Survivors. O formato segue o estilo de sobrevivência, no qual os ataques acontecem de forma automática e o foco está na movimentação pelo cenário, enquanto o jogador enfrenta hordas contínuas de inimigos em arenas fechadas. O título reúne mais de 40 campeões extraídos dos universos de Warhammer 40,000 e Warhammer Age of Sigmar. Durante as partidas, é necessário coletar recursos deixados pelos oponentes derrotados para subir de nível e escolher novas armas e habilidades. O game ainda não possui um preço definido, mas já conta com uma versão demo que pode ser baixada de forma gratuita. Sonic Pico Park é um jogo de ação e quebra-cabeça focado no modo multijogador cooperativo. A proposta une os personagens da franquia do ouriço da Sega com as mecânicas de colaboração em grupo vistas no título independente Pico Park original. Para completar cada fase, os participantes precisam coordenar seus movimentos e realizar ações conjuntas, como empilhar os personagens para alcançar locais mais altos ou ativar botões simultaneamente. O progresso exige comunicação constante entre os jogadores , pois falhas individuais resultam no reinício do nível atual. O jogo ainda não possui um preço definido. Barbie Rewind é uma coletânea focada na preservação histórica de títulos antigos da boneca da Mattel, desenvolvida pela Digital Eclipse e publicada pela Atari. O pacote conta com os seguintes jogos: Seguindo o modelo de outros projetos da desenvolvedora, a coleção funciona como um museu virtual interativo, trazendo artes conceituais, documentos de bastidores e materiais de acervo sobre o desenvolvimento dos jogos. O game ainda não possui um preço definido. E na sua opinião, qual o game mais esperado da semana? Conte para a gente nas redes sociais do Voxel!
